title: Show the reader any named job's request and findings
summary: Today only 'try again on <job>' (rejected jobs only) gives the reader the earlier job's request and findings. I read the request as: any request that names a full job id gets that job's request and findings in the reader brief, while the retry form keeps working.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and lifecycle tests for referenced-job detection and brief rendering.
Read the existing 'try again on' implementation to infer the intended generalization.
Extend the existing earlier-attempt mechanism rather than adding a new subsystem.
Carried text goes through the redactor.

assumptions: Naming means a full job id (like 20261012-075824-1x28) matched by its format, to avoid false matches on ordinary words; unique suffixes are only resolved in the 'try again on' form.
Any job state is shown, not only rejected; the retry form keeps its rejected-only rule.
The number of referenced jobs is capped to bound brief size.
The brief shows the referenced job's request and findings as quoted data; the new request takes precedence.
question: Should a bare job-id suffix (not the full id) also count as naming a job outside 'try again on'? I assumed only full ids do.

acceptance_criteria.text: A request that contains a full job id anywhere in its text (not only after 'try again on') causes the reader brief to include that job's request and its final verification findings and reasons, redacted like the retry path.

Jobs in any state with a request record are shown; a job with no verification gets only its request. An id that does not resolve is ignored, not an error, unless the request uses the 'try again on' form.

'try again on <job>' still works: refuses landed or unknown jobs and carries a rejected job's request and findings. Run cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle and cargo test for athena-core and athena-context.

New tests cover the brief rendering for a referenced job and detection of ids mid-sentence, and a lifecycle test shows a non-retry request naming a job gets its request and findings in the reader brief. Run cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo fmt --check.
README.md and CHANGELOG.md describe the behavior.

out_of_scope: Resolving unique id suffixes outside the 'try again on' form
Changing the producer or verifier briefs
Changing record formats or governance files
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference: touches two crates plus tests and docs, and the semantics are underspecified.
